run: # The shell is deliberately left running. This script is a child of Arbitrium, which
# is always elevated, so everything it starts inherits an administrator token —

# script cannot start the shell again as anything but an administrator, so it must not

run: # This action is the one that had the whole bug in it. It stopped the shell because
# Explorer holds iconcache_*.db and thumbcache_*.db open, and then started explorer.exe
# again from this elevated PowerShell — which is precisely what cannot work: a process
# started from here inherits Arbitrium's administrator token, and Explorer does not take
# the shell role with one. It hands that job to a scheduled task that starts it again
# unelevated, and that task is created on demand, can be disabled, and is exactly the
# sort of thing a debloating pass removes. Where it was missing, an action about icons
# left the user with no desktop and nothing on screen to fix it with.
# So the shell is left alone and the work is split in two. The files that are not
# locked go now; ie4uinit is Windows' own way to make the running shell drop and rebuild
# its icon cache without stopping anything (-show is the Windows 10 and 11 spelling of
# what was -ClearIconCache on 7); and the databases Explorer is holding open are freed
# the next time the shell restarts, which is the apply overlay's button and is verified.
# Both directories are asked of the API rather than read out of the environment, for
# the same reason shell.cpp calls GetWindowsDirectoryW instead of trusting PATH. This
# script is a child of a process that always runs as administrator and inherits its
# environment block from whoever launched it, so $Env:SystemRoot and $Env:LocalAppData
# are values somebody else may have chosen. GetFolderPath and SystemDirectory are not:
# one of these lines runs an executable, and three of them delete files by wildcard.

actions.name: Yeniden başlat
actions.desc: Makineyi hemen yeniden başlatır.
actions.note: Geri sayım yoktur: onayladığınız anda başlar. Kaydedilmemiş çalışmalarınız kaybolur.
run: # Nothing is printed after this line and there is no ARB result token, because the
# machine is gone before PowerShell could print one. actionpage.cpp:48 falls back to
# actions.status.* for an empty output, which is the right sentence for a restart.
# A native tool's failure is not a PowerShell error, so $ErrorActionPreference does
# not catch it. Without this guard a refused restart - another shutdown already

# report a restart that is not going to happen.

Kaydedilmemiş çalışmalarınız kaybolur.
run: # The braces are quoted, and that is not cosmetic. PowerShell reads a bare {current}
